_comment: A crossplane inline four, of the sort Yamaha put in the R1: 998 cc, four
cylinders in a row, but with the crankpins at 0/90/270/180 instead of the
usual 0/180/180/0. It fires at 270-180-90-180 degrees rather than evenly,
which is why it sounds like a V-twin with a stutter instead of like a
Nothing here is code. This is the shape an engine takes when it lives in a
game's content pipeline: load the JSON, hand it straight to
createEngineSound. The crossplane firing pattern is not written down —
it falls out of the journal angles and the firing order below.
Units are SI throughout: metres, cubic metres, radians, rad/s, newton
metres. See js/README.md for what each field means.
name: Crossplane Inline Four
_firingOrderComment: 1-2-4-3. With those journal angles this lands on 0, 270, 450 and 540 degrees.

params._chamberVolume: 21 cc, which is 12.9:1 on a 249.5 cc cylinder
params._breathing: Individual throttle bodies, sized for one litre at 12000 rpm.
params._inertia: A motorcycle crank is light, so it picks up and drops fast.
params._windage: Multiplies omega squared, so it is a small number: at the
params._windage2: limiter this is about 47 Nm. Roughly 0.03 x displacement.

cam._comment: Short duration, high lift, as a high-revving four wants.

portFlow._comment: Valve lift in metres against flow-bench SCFM at 28 inH2O.

audio._comment: A bike engine with no bodywork: hard-edged and busy.
